To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is possible to grow single-phase chalcopyrite films at low temperatures by the thermal evaporation of compounds.
it is possible to prepare chalcopyrite films by thermal evaporating compound materials.
it was possible to prepare high quality Cu(In,Ga)(S,Se)2 thin film solar cells with an efficiency of 14.4% by using a novel thermal evaporation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation, characterization and device fabrication of chalcopyrite-based thin-film solar cells.
the development of new and innovative approaches for the fabrication of thin films of CuInSe2, CuGaSe2 and CuInxGa1-xSe2 for the application in solar cells.
the development of a new approach for the preparation of chalcopyrite compound thin films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
compound chalcopyrites can be evaporated in a controlled manner and the resulting films are of good quality.
the compound evaporation approach is an attractive alternative to the more conventional flash evaporation method.

the use of compound materials for the growth of chalcopyrite films has the potential of becoming a viable alternative to the commonly used two-source evaporation technique, especially when device quality films are required at low substrate temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it has been possible to produce device quality chal-copyrite thin films by the slow evaporation of compound source materials.
we have developed a new method for the production of high quality chalcopyrites.
the thermal evaporation of chalcopyrite compound materials is a promising approach for the production of thin films with device quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to prepare high quality CuInSe2 absorber layers by thermal evaporation at relatively low substrate temperatures, and that the same is not possible with the Cu(In,Ga)(Se,Te)2 system.
the flash-evaporated chalcopyrite films are of a quality comparable to those obtained by co-evaporation of the constituent elements, and the flash-evaporative approach is more cost-effective.
the thermal evaporation of chalcopyrite compounds is an excellent technique for the preparation of device-quality chalcopyrite films.
